Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of key clinical findings and impressions:  
  - Patient presents with 2 days of central/suprapubic lower abdominal pain, mild nausea, subjective hot/sweaty sensation, self-measured temperature ~37°C, reported slight visible hematuria and mildly increased urinary frequency. No dysuria, no flank/back pain, no vaginal discharge, no vomiting. No significant past medical history recorded. Allergy to amoxicillin documented. Lives with parents; drinks alcohol moderately.  
- Working diagnosis (supported by transcript and DDx):  
  - Acute lower urinary tract infection (cystitis) — Working diagnosis (High likelihood). Justification: suprapubic pain, visible hematuria, increased urinary frequency and mild systemic symptoms; aligns with clinician impression in transcript and DDx ranking.  
- Management documented in transcript:  
  - Clinician recommended a short course of oral antibiotics (three-day course, twice daily) to be sent to the pharmacy; patient agreed.  
  - Advice given to seek urgent review if pain worsens, develops high temperature, back/flank pain, new symptoms, or if not improving — may require face-to-face assessment.  
  - Note: patient allergic to amoxicillin — antibiotic choice should avoid amoxicillin (conflict/alert for prescribing).  
- Relevant differentials from DDx consistent with transcript:  
  - Ureteric/renal stone (Medium likelihood): Hematuria plus acute lower abdominal pain support consideration; absence of flank colicky pain and severe pain makes this less likely but possible.  
  - Gynecologic causes (ovarian cyst rupture/torsion, PID, ectopic pregnancy) (Medium likelihood overall): Lower abdominal pain and nausea could be gynecologic; contraceptive implant history is ambiguous so pregnancy/ectopic should be excluded with a urine pregnancy test. Lack of vaginal bleeding/discharge and central pain reduce likelihood of some gynecologic diagnoses.  
  - Appendicitis (Low likelihood): Central lower abdominal pain and mild systemic features could represent early/atypical appendicitis; less likely given suprapubic predominance and current clinical picture.  
- Considerations and recommended further investigations/actions (consistent with transcript and DDx):  
  - Urine dipstick and microscopy ± urine culture to confirm UTI and guide antibiotic choice.  
  - Pregnancy test (urine) to exclude pregnancy/ectopic given ambiguous contraceptive history.  
  - If hematuria persists or stone suspected, consider renal imaging (non-contrast CT or ultrasound) and urology input.  
  - If severe localized unilateral adnexal pain, concern for ovarian torsion — arrange urgent gynecologic review and pelvic ultrasound.  
  - Avoid prescribing amoxicillin due to documented allergy.  
- Conflicts / important alerts:  
  - Allergy to amoxicillin documented; clinician recommended antibiotics but did not document specific agent — prescribing must account for allergy (conflict noted).  
  - Contraceptive implant status ambiguous in transcript and DDx (implant described but current status unclear) — pregnancy risk unclear (conflict noted).
